To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conformational change in a metallo-beta-lacatamase active site alpha-helix is not a consequence of the formation of a substrate-metal complex, but instead represents a distinct step of the reaction with the substrate.

(i) conformational change in the metallo-β-lactamase, ImiS, accompanies formation of a transient intermediate during the reaction with the substrate impiemen, and that (ii) in a subpopulation of Imis molecules, this conformation change is not associated with substrate-binding to the active site metals, but rather, is a separate step in the reaction mechanism.

the binding of the beta-lactam antibiotic imipenem to the class B2 beta-lactamase enzyme ImiS is associated with a conformational movement that is not associated with binding to the active-site metal ion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and dynamics of metallo-beta-lacatamases, which are enzymes that confer antibiotic resistance on certain bacteria.
the study of the structure and function of metallo-beta-lactalases, enzymes which are important in the development of antibiotic resistance in pathogenic bacteria.

the study of the mechanisms of metallo-enzymes, with a particular emphasis on metallo-beta-lacatamases, the enzymes responsible for conferring resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics in pathogenic bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a novel and important finding.

the conformational changes observed in this study are not associated with substrate or inhibitor binding to the active metal ion, but rather are associated with the reaction of the substrate with the metal ion.

the binding of the substrate to the active site of the enzyme is not the only factor that determines its specificity, but the conformational change that occurs upon binding is also a significant factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metal binding site of ImiS undergoes conformational changes upon the binding of substrated and/or inhibitors, and these changes can be observed using EPR spectrokinetics of spin-labeled mutants.
the conformational changes of metallo-beta-lacatmases are not only important for the substrate binding but also for the catalytic mechanism.
the conformational changes of the active site metallo-beta-lactalase ImiS are important in the catalytic reaction and the substrate binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that

conformational change is an important part of the reaction catalyzed by metallo-beta-lacatamases, and this conformational rearrangement is not necessarily associated with binding to the active-site metal ions.

the substrate binding to the metal ion is not the only step that is rate determining in the reaction of ImiS with imipenem, and that the conformational change we observed in our study is not necessarily coupled to the binding of the substrate to the metal ion.
the binding of a substrate or inhibitor to a metallo-beta-lacatamase may not be accompanied by binding to one or both of the metal ions in the active site.
